title: Measuring the Later Earnings of a Keyturn Host Payout Account
content:
Which earnings count as later on a Keyturn Host Payout Account turns on how the account settles and on whether money has lately left the account.

**Where the account is swept as each trip completes and a transfer has left it in the three months up to that day**, the trip earnings credited in the twelve months up to that day count as later.

**Where the account is swept as each trip completes and no transfer has left it in that period**, the trip earnings credited in the three months up to that day count as later.

**In every other case**, only the trip earnings credited in the month up to that day count as later.

## Points of judgement

**An account swept as each trip completes that has paid something out this quarter.** The first case governs, and the stretch measured is the twelve months up to that day.

**The same account with nothing paid out in the three months up to that day.** The second case governs, and the stretch narrows to those three months.

**An account settling on any other rhythm.** The third case governs whatever has left it, and only the month up to that day is measured.

## On hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical account credited with trip earnings of 9000.00 USD in the twelve months up to that day, 2400.00 USD in the three months up to that day and 800.00 USD in the month up to that day. The later earnings are 9000.00 USD in the first case, 2400.00 USD in the second and 800.00 USD in the third.

The records that settle it are the account's own ledger: the transfers released from it in the three months up to that day, and the trip earning entries credited to it over each of the three stretches.
